name: DataForSEO
verdict: No OAuth and no customer connection: it is a data vendor your product calls server-side with its own credentials after a $50 minimum top-up. A customer who wants their own account pastes their API login and password.
needGuide: No — just keep your own API login and password server-side, and collect a customer's only if they bring their own account.

auth.detail: HTTP Basic auth only: Base64 of the API login and API password (separate from the account password) in the Authorization header; credentials cannot be passed as URL parameters. No OAuth and no token exchange. The sandbox uses the same credentials.

approval.gate: No OAuth exists, so no approval gate. Your own production use only needs a funded account: $50 minimum top-up, pay-as-you-go, funds do not expire. No partner program or app review is documented. DataForSEO is a data vendor your product pays for, not an account your customers connect, so call it server-side with your own credentials.

scopes.why: No scopes: the credentials reach every API the funded balance pays for.
scopes.summary: No scopes. The credentials grant access to every API the funded balance can pay for. Per-key limits or sub-accounts were not confirmed.

cost: Pay-as-you-go, $50 minimum top-up; $1 trial credit for new accounts; sandbox free
prerequisites: Account and owner: Whoever signs up owns the API credentials; use a company-owned login rather than a personal one. Team roles were not documented in the pages read.
Where you register: Sign up at app.dataforseo.com/register, then open the API Access page to see your API login and password
Cost: Pay-as-you-go, $50 minimum top-up; $1 trial credit for new accounts; sandbox free

registerAt.path: Sign up at app.dataforseo.com/register, then open the API Access page to see your API login and password

steps.do: Register at app.dataforseo.com/register using a company email
Open app.dataforseo.com/api-access and copy the API login and password into your secrets manager
Build requests against https://sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3 using Basic auth (Base64 of login:password)
Verify task_post with pingback_url and postback_url handlers against the sandbox
Add the $50 minimum top-up to the account
Switch the base URL to api.dataforseo.com and run a small live smoke test; set spend alerts in your app

roles.team: Whoever signs up owns the API credentials; use a company-owned login rather than a personal one. Team roles were not documented in the pages read.
roles.customer: None for the normal case. If a customer wants to use their own DataForSEO account, they paste their API login and password into your app; store them encrypted.

testing: Swap api.dataforseo.com/v3 for sandbox.dataforseo.com/v3 with the same login and password.
It is free for any registered user, returns dummy data in the production response shape, supports pingback_url and postback_url, and has the same rate limits (10,000 calls/min).
The $1 trial credit covers a few live calls (Playground, MCP, templates).

blockers.problem: The API password differs from the account password
blockers.fix: 401 errors usually mean the wrong one. Copy both from the API Access page.
A leak can drain the balance. Keep calls server-side and avoid large balances or auto top-up.
It cannot validate result quality. Use the $1 trial credit for a few live checks.

blockers.problem: Live methods take one task per POST
blockers.fix: Use task_post with pingback for volume.

automation.agentCan: Write the Basic-auth client (official PHP, C#, Java, Python and TypeScript libraries, an OpenAPI spec and a Postman collection exist), run sandbox test calls, and add retry and cost-tracking logic.
automation.humanMust: Create the account, accept the terms, pay the top-up, and retrieve the credentials from the console.

uncertain: Sub-account or per-key spend limits, any partner or reseller program, MCP server auth details, and terms for reselling data to third parties were not confirmed.
